subject.title: [Feature]: Feature Request: Batch Tool Calls + Context Block Management + Plan Enforcement

question: Should OpenClaw keep this umbrella and split it into native tool batching, context block lifecycle, and plan/workflow enforcement tracks, and which pieces belong in core runtime/API versus plugin or ClawHub surfaces?
rationale: The request adds native tool schemas, persisted context semantics, new config/settings, and runner enforcement policy; repository policy treats those as compatibility- and product-sensitive choices rather than a narrow repair.

options.title: Split Into Design Tracks
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and require separate maintainer-reviewed designs for batching, context lifecycle, and plan enforcement before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Canonical Issues
options.body: Use the existing context and enforcement issues for their portions and open or retain a separate focused tracker for native batch tool calls.

options.title: Reject Broad Core Orchestration
options.body: Close or sharply narrow the umbrella if maintainers decide AI-controlled context swapping and strict plan enforcement are too much orchestration for core.

recommendation.title: Split Into Design Tracks
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and require separate maintainer-reviewed designs for batching, context lifecycle, and plan enforcement before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the broadest adjacent history across planning, strict-agentic execution, web/search tooling, and context pruning, making it the best available routing owner for the product split.
